reasoning: The PR passes themeOverrides={{ oddRowBackgroundColor: theme.colorBgLayout }} to ThemedAgGridReact, replacing the default odd-row colour theme.colorFillQuaternary. In the light theme this raises stripe contrast (1.0438 -> 1.0902) and reproduces the classic table chart exactly (#f5f5f5 over #ffffff). In the dark theme (supersetDark) colorBgLayout resolves to #000000, which is identical to the AG Grid surface the rows are painted on (--ag-background-color: #000), so the zebra striping disappears completely: measured painted odd/even row colours are both rgb(0,0,0) and stripe contrast drops from 1.0607 on base to 1.0000 on the PR. Losing the row-tracking affordance entirely in one of the two shipped themes is a rendering regression, so the gate fails despite the light-theme improvement. The change also does not achieve the parity it claims in dark mode: the classic table still stripes in dark (1.1399, #000000 odd rows over a #141414 container surface) because its unstriped rows sit on colorBgContainer, whereas AG Grid's base surface is the page background itself.

components_inspected.component: plugins/plugin-chart-table TableChart (reference for the look the PR aims to match)

evidence.method: Storybook dev server on localhost:6006, stories loaded in Playwright/Chromium at viewport 1200x800, deviceScaleFactor 1. For each AG Grid row the computed background-color was read from the DOM, and the painted colour was sampled from the full-page screenshot at the row's vertical centre in an empty part of the first column (x = row.left + 180). Stripe contrast is the WCAG relative-luminance contrast ratio between the painted even-row and odd-row colours. Base and PR were rendered from the same Storybook instance with the same local-only story data fix (see local_only_story_adjustment).

local_only_story_adjustment: superset-frontend/plugins/plugin-chart-ag-grid-table/src/stories/AgGridTable.stories.tsx does not render on master or on the PR branch: transformProps throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'forEach') at chartProps.datasource.metrics.forEach because the story's datasource has no metrics/columns. metrics: [] and columns: [] were added to the story datasource locally to make it render. This adjustment was applied identically to both branches and was not committed.
